summary:
Audit of web-01, db-01 and ci-01 after the 14:28 UTC restore. I found no confirmed unauthorized login, no webshell or new PHP in uploads, no new DB users, no changed release or backup scripts, and no tampering with the repo or the release. The release (ci-01 -> web-01) and dumps (db-01 -> ci-01) run normally, and the payout check and settle job pass.

Noise, not compromise: a steady flow of SSH brute force and scanning from many internet IPs (3.236.x, 54.36.41.216, 194.165.243.16, 174.53.99.180, 218.92.71.16, 148.251.40.94, 159.89.x and others) for root, test, pi, hadoop, postgres, git, debian, nagios, ftpuser and similar names. All of these failed. Web probes (wp-config.php.bak, eval-stdin.php, /admin/config.php) got 404s. The POSTs to inc/availability.php came from ordinary browsers on the rentals page, which is normal booking traffic.

Not proven, needs your check: (1) nvega's key was used once from 172.58.17.252 (a mobile carrier address never seen before) on web-01 at 14:33; (2) mfischer logged in with a password from 107.77.170.208 at 14:31, a new address (her usual is 67.180.67.206); (3) several staff logged in with passwords from the office IP 98.212.158.167 at 14:30-14:32 (hgrant, plus jcole and pshah on other days). These may be legitimate. I did not rotate any secret because I found no evidence that one was read by someone unauthorized.

Weaknesses found and closed:
- web-01: account jpark (contractor, NOT in /etc/larkspur/staff.txt) had a password that never expires, was in the sudo group (passwordless root) and had no successful logins. I locked it, set its shell to nologin and removed it from sudo. If it is a real contractor, re-enable it and add it to staff.txt.
- web-01 and ci-01 and db-01: the sudoers rule '%sudo ALL=(ALL:ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL' (passwordless root for everyone in the sudo group, including the contractor DBA rnakamura on db-01) is removed. The admins still have sudo, but now it asks for their password. Please check that mreyes and nvega can sudo.
- web-01: 'deploy ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/rsync' (the shared deploy account could become root through rsync) is removed. Nothing in the scripts uses it; the release still runs.
- Backups of the old sudoers files are in /root/sudoers-backup-1450 on web-01 and ci-01 and db-01.

Still open for Maria:
- ci-01: the GitHub token of the repo is stored in plaintext in /srv/git/larkspur-site.git/config, and that file is readable by the 'developers' group, which includes the contractor agarcia. Not rotated, because rotating it needs GitHub and the group permissions need a decision that won't break pushes. Recommend rotating it (rotate-secret deploy-token) and moving it into a credential helper.
- The shared deploy account's password and the old SSH password logins for staff remain. Staff still log in with passwords (I did not disable them, to avoid locking people out). Recommend keys-only once staff have keys.
- web-01: the restored plugin repo has an extra commit (77aa63e, made from the web-01 copy at 14:30) that is not on ci-01's repo; check this against the release.

Confirmed unauthorized access to web-01 through the shared deploy account. Someone outside the shop (35.196.129.99, a Google Cloud address; not in staff.txt) logged in with the deploy account's password about 60 times between 1 Nov and 14:34 today, most recently at 14:34:47. The deploy password was used once more from 172.58.183.223 on 9 Nov. Maria's own IP (50.39.81.213) also logged in as deploy with the password a few times, so the password is in use by people and old scripts. The 14:34 session ran a command and closed; I could not see what it did. I found no other changes: the plugin git tree is clean, no PHP was added to uploads, the deploy authorized_keys is unchanged (one key), and ci-01 has no password logins for deploy. The release and the dumps are still running.

Containment done on web-01:
- Password logins are now refused for the deploy account only (sshd drop-in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/90-deploy-keyonly.conf, sshd reloaded). The CI release uses its key from ci-01 and is unaffected. 
- rotate-secret deploy-password: the old password no longer works. Maria's and any old scripts' deploy logins will fail until the help desk hands out the new password (about 8 minutes). Use mreyes with sudo instead, or get the new password from the help desk.
- Earlier today: locked the unlisted account jpark, removed the passwordless %sudo rule on all three servers, removed the deploy rsync-as-root rule on web-01 (sudoers backups are in /root/sudoers-backup-1450 on each host).

Still to check (not confirmed as attacks, so not rotated): lucia logged in 11 times with a password from 172.58.157.83 (a mobile address) and wlin logged in 15 times with her key from 71.58.189.55, both today. Please confirm with them. nvega's key from the new mobile address 172.58.17.252 and mfischer's password from 107.77.170.208 at 14:31-14:35 need confirming too.

Recommended next: check what the attacker could reach with the deploy account (the larkspur-deploy sudo script, the plugin, and wp-config for DB access), review the 14:34 session, and rotate the GitHub token in the ci-01 repo config (readable by the developers group). Move the deploy account to key-only for everyone, and keep password logins only for named staff.

Unauthorized access to web-01 through the shared deploy account, from 35.196.129.99 (about 60 password logins from 1 Nov to 14:34 today) and once from 172.58.183.223 on 9 Nov. Containment is in place: password logins for deploy are refused on web-01 (sshd drop-in 90-deploy-keyonly.conf), and the deploy password was rotated. The CI release from ci-01 uses its key and is still running ok. ci-01 and db-01 show no password logins for deploy.

What the attacker could reach: deploy has passwordless sudo for only three root helper scripts (larkspur-deploy, larkspur-restart, and the earlier rsync rule, now removed). I read those scripts; their arguments are only echoed, and they cannot be changed by deploy. I found no changed or added files that the attacker could have written: the plugin git tree is clean; the root-owned wp binary and acme-poscollect predate today; the deploy and mreyes authorized_keys are unchanged; payments.ini is root-only and was not reachable, so I did not rotate the payment key; there are no new cron entries. The 14:34 session ran a command and closed, and its contents are not visible in the logs. Because the attacker's sessions were command-only and short, I cannot rule out that they read files as deploy. Treat the deploy password as having been known to outsiders for about two weeks, and check whatever the deploy account can read on web-01.

Other changes made today: jpark locked and removed from sudo; passwordless %sudo removed on all three hosts (backups in /root/sudoers-backup-1450); deploy rsync-as-root removed on web-01.

Not confirmed as attacks: lucia (11 password logins from 172.58.157.83), wlin (15 key logins from 71.58.189.55), nvega (key from 172.58.17.252), mfischer (password from 107.77.170.208). Please confirm each with the person. Maria's own password login as deploy will now fail; use her own account with sudo, or get the new password from the help desk.

Still open: the GitHub token in the ci-01 repo config is readable by the developers group and should be rotated; and other staff still use password logins (not disabled, to avoid lockouts).

Update. Unauthorized access to web-01 through the shared deploy account (from 35.196.129.99, about 60 password logins from 1 Nov to 14:34 today; once from 172.58.183.223 on 9 Nov). Contained: deploy password logins refused, deploy password rotated. No deploy password logins since.

New: the deploy account can read /var/www/larkspur/wp-config.php (group www-data), so the WordPress database password was exposed to the attacker. I rotated it with rotate-secret app-db-password. The site returns 200, and the orders job is ok. The weekly report job (which keeps its own copy in /etc/larkspur/report.cnf) was failing, so I updated that copy (root-only, verified ok at 14:42) and deleted my backup that held the old value. The payment key and the billing password are root-only (payments.ini) and the attacker could not read them, so I did not rotate them. Grafana, restic and the redis cache password are also not readable by deploy.

Checked and clean: no changed or new files the attacker could have written; the plugin is clean; the root-owned wp binary and the POS tool are from the 3 Nov build; no new cron entries. The 14:34 deploy session ran a command and closed, and I cannot see what it ran. Please treat the deploy account's readable files on web-01 as seen by outsiders.

Other changes today: jpark locked and removed from sudo; passwordless %sudo removed on all three hosts (backups in /root/sudoers-backup-1450); deploy rsync-as-root removed on web-01.

Still to confirm with the people involved (not confirmed as attacks): lucia (password from 172.58.157.83, 11 times), wlin (key from 71.58.189.55, 15 times), nvega (key from 172.58.17.252), mfischer (password from 107.77.170.208).

Still open: the GitHub token in the ci-01 repo config is readable by the developers group, and should be rotated when the team is ready (rotate-secret deploy-token, which also needs the GitHub side changed). Staff password logins are still allowed, to avoid lockouts. Maria's own deploy login will fail until she gets the new password from the help desk; she can use her own account with sudo meanwhile.

Final check on the web-01 deploy compromise. The sudo log shows that deploy ran only the CI release helper (larkspur-deploy 883881f) through sudo, across all of its history. The attacker never ran a privileged command as deploy. The only other deploy-sudo entries are my own access tests at 14:38 (restic password, WordPress config), which failed. Their non-sudo shell commands (the 14:34 session) are not visible in the logs.

Containment, unchanged from the last report: deploy password logins are refused on web-01 and the deploy password is rotated; the WordPress database password is rotated (wp-config.php is readable by deploy, so it was exposed); the report job's copy of that password is updated and the job is ok; my backup of the old value is deleted. Nothing else readable by deploy was rotated (payments.ini, grafana.ini and the restic password are root-only).

Still to confirm with the people involved: lucia (password from 172.58.157.83), wlin (key from 71.58.189.55), nvega (key from 172.58.17.252), mfischer (password from 107.77.170.208). Still open: the GitHub token in ci-01's repo config (readable by developers); password logins for staff (kept, to avoid lockouts).

Final state at 14:44 UTC. Containment on web-01 is holding: deploy password logins refused, deploy and WordPress database passwords rotated, no further attacker logins. The site (200), payouts, orders, report, release (ci-01), maintenance, dumps and settlement are all ok.

Please check: on db-01 at 14:33:44, mreyes corrected invoice 11 from 110500 to 103000 cents (order LC-201) with the bookkeeping script. Probably Maria's own change, since she logged in to db-01 at 14:33, but I could not verify it.

Still to confirm with the people involved: lucia (password from 172.58.157.83), wlin (key from 71.58.189.55), nvega (key from 172.58.17.252), mfischer (password from 107.77.170.208). Still open: the GitHub token in ci-01's repo config (readable by developers) should be rotated; staff password logins are still allowed to avoid lockouts; Maria's password login as deploy will fail until she gets the new password from the help desk.
